docs_facts.fact: CLAUDE.md files are plain-markdown instructions loaded into context at session start. They are context, not enforced configuration, so a PreToolUse hook is the tool for hard blocks. Files from the directory tree above the working directory are concatenated (root first, working directory last), not overridden; files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude touches files there. Target under 200 lines per file; @path imports expand into context but do not cut its cost (max four hops). Block-level HTML comments are stripped before injection. Repos using AGENTS.md can have it read in place of CLAUDE.md.

The user-level instructions file, applying to all your projects; it loads before project files so project text appears later in context. Other scopes: managed policy file (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md), project ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, and personal per-project ./CLAUDE.local.md. Imports in user-scope files load without the external-import approval dialog that project files trigger.

Project-local personal settings file at .claude/settings.local.json. It outranks the shared .claude/settings.json and user ~/.claude/settings.json, and is outranked only by command-line --settings and managed settings. Claude Code writes 'don't ask again' approvals into it and adds it to the global git excludes; a hand-made copy must be gitignored manually. Since v2.1.211 in a git repo the file lives at the repository root. Its allow rules skip the workspace-trust step while the file is untracked.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Precedence order and file location are version-sensitive (location rule changed at v2.1.211); older study material may place the file in the start directory.

docs_facts.fact: Six modes: default (alias manual), acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions. Set with --permission-mode, Shift+Tab (except dontAsk, flag/config only), or permissions.defaultMode. Start-mode precedence: flag, then defaultMode in settings (project-level auto and bypassPermissions values ignored), then built-in default. Built-in default is auto for interactive terminal/VS Code on v2.1.283+ and default for claude -p and the Agent SDK.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Interactive default became auto (v2.1.283+) and -p/SDK runs with no mode set start in Manual and deny calls needing approval (v2.1.302). Older material says default prompts everywhere or that -p is permissive.

docs_facts.fact: Plan mode lets Claude explore and propose without editing source until you approve the plan. With auto mode available and useAutoModeDuringPlan on (default), a classifier reviews shell commands during planning. A PreToolUse hook allow does not approve edits in plan mode. In interactive terminal sessions with bypass permissions available, planning is not enforced. Enter via --permission-mode plan, Shift+Tab, or /plan.

Skips prompts and most safety checks, including writes to protected paths such as .git and .claude. Deny rules and explicit ask rules still apply, and allow rules have no effect. It still prompts or denies for critical-path rm/rmdir, AskUserQuestion, and requiresUserInteraction MCP tools. You cannot switch into it mid-session unless the session started with it enabled; it is refused as root on Linux/macOS outside a sandbox and ignored from project/local settings defaultMode. Org kill switch: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode set to disable.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Before v2.1.257 bypassPermissions took effect from any settings file; now it does not take effect from project or local settings.

docs_facts.fact: Auto-denies every call that would otherwise prompt; reads in working directories, read-only Bash, and anything matching permissions.allow still run. AskUserQuestion, org-ask connector tools, and requiresUserInteraction MCP tools are denied even if allowed. Not in the Shift+Tab cycle (flag or config only). Intended for CI and locked-down scripts.

Deny-rule flag (--disallowedTools or --disallowed-tools). A bare tool name removes the tool from Claude's context entirely; a scoped rule such as Bash(rm *) keeps the tool and denies only matching calls as written. Deny rules from any scope beat allow rules, and a managed deny cannot be lifted by --allowedTools. The same name appears as disallowedTools in subagent frontmatter and SDK options.

Allow-rule list (--allowedTools / --allowed-tools, or allowed_tools/allowedTools in the SDK). It auto-approves the listed tools but does not restrict the others; use --tools to restrict availability. Evaluation order in Claude Code is deny, then ask, then allow, first match wins, with no specificity override. In bypassPermissions mode allowed_tools does not constrain anything.

Runs before a tool call. Input on stdin carries hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id plus common fields (session_id, cwd, permission_mode). Output goes in stdout JSON under hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName PreToolUse. Exit 2 blocks the call and stderr becomes the reason, even if JSON said allow; other non-zero codes are non-blocking errors. A hook allow does not bypass deny or ask rules. Hook handler types: command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent (experimental).
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Hook event list has grown (PostToolBatch, PermissionDenied, PreModelSwitch, etc.); older material lists far fewer events.

docs_facts.fact: PreToolUse field inside hookSpecificOutput. Values: allow, deny, ask, defer. permissionDecisionReason is shown to Claude (and the user on deny/ask). PermissionRequest hooks use a different shape, hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior with allow or deny.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: The 'defer' value is not in older descriptions that list only allow/deny/ask. Whether the old top-level approve/block form for PreToolUse is deprecated: not verified (page excerpt silent).

docs_facts.fact: A PreToolUse hook can rewrite the tool's arguments by returning updatedInput directly under hookSpecificOutput; it replaces the arguments before the tool runs. In plan mode Claude Code still applies a returned updatedInput even though a hook allow does not approve edits.

allowed-tools lists tools usable without prompting while the skill's turn is active; it does not restrict other tools (disallowed-tools removes tools from the pool instead). Other frontmatter fields: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, model, effort, context (fork), agent, background, hooks, paths, shell. Unrecognised fields are ignored silently. Outside Claude Code only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools are accepted by the Agent Skills spec.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Custom commands (.claude/commands/) have been merged into skills; a skill beats a same-named command file.

docs_facts.fact: Set to true so only the user can invoke the skill (via /name); Claude will not load it automatically, and its description is not added to the per-turn listing. Default false. The opposite switch, user-invocable: false, hides the skill from the / menu so only Claude invokes it. Listing text (description plus when_to_use) is truncated at 1,536 characters; keep SKILL.md under 500 lines.

A plugin bundles skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers (and optionally a JS hooks module, making it a mod) installed as one unit. Manifest at .claude-plugin/plugin.json; a marketplace is a repo with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Install via /plugin or claude plugin; develop locally with --plugin-dir. Install scopes: user, project (committed .claude/settings.json), local. Plugin skills are namespaced as /plugin:skill. Orgs can allowlist/block marketplaces via managed settings.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: The 'mods' concept (plugin with a JS hooks module) is recent and likely absent from older material.

docs_facts.fact: Anthropic's agentic coding tool; the same agent loop and tools are exposed as the Agent SDK and the claude -p CLI. Detailed product-overview page was not fetched; only facts from the CLI, settings and SDK pages are recorded in other entries.

-p/--print runs non-interactively and exits (0 on success, non-zero on failure). Pipe data via stdin (capped at 10MB). --bare skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md for reproducible scripted runs and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (no OAuth); the docs say it will become the default for -p. Continue with -c/--continue or --resume <session_id>. --max-turns and --max-budget-usd are print-mode only; --no-session-persistence is print-mode only. SIGTERM exits 143.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Since v2.1.302 a -p run with no permission mode starts in Manual (denies calls needing approval); --bare is slated to become the -p default.

docs_facts.fact: --output-format accepts text (default), json, stream-json. json returns one object with the text in result, plus session_id, usage and total_cost_usd with a per-model cost breakdown. stream-json emits newline-delimited events and needs --verbose (and --include-partial-messages for token deltas); the last line is a result message; system/init lists tools, mcp_servers, plugins; system/api_retry reports retries; denials appear as permission_denials. --input-format accepts text or stream-json.

Print-mode flag; combine with --output-format json to get schema-validated output in the structured_output field of the JSON response. If the run ends without valid structured output (for example a refusal) the field is absent, so check for it before use. An invalid schema exits with an error; the format keyword is accepted but only annotation, not enforced.

Glob is a built-in tool name accepted in allowedTools and subagent tools (e.g. read-only sets Read, Grep, Glob). Behaviour, limits and permission semantics of Glob itself: not verified (tools-reference page not fetched).
